bug_semantics: phpMyFAQ's authenticated content-backup API (BackupController::download type=content, gated by PermissionType::BACKUP) built a ZipArchive of PMF_CONTENT_DIR — including content/core/config/database.php — at the web-accessible document-root path PMF_ROOT_DIR/content.zip, then streamed the file and unlinked it. Unlike archives under content/, that root path is not blocked by content/.htaccess. An unauthenticated client can race GET /content.zip during the write-to-unlink window (or fetch a leftover archive after a failed unlink) and obtain database credentials and other content/. With admin-context XSS, an attacker can trigger the authenticated backup from the victim session and then fetch content.zip without holding BACKUP themselves.
flaw_origin: The insecure location was first written on 2024-06-16 in PR #3003 member d28770dc075c5d7d220f7c540e4cdd8620724930 (Jan / @modelrailroader): Backup::createContentFolderBackup() set $zipFile = PMF_ROOT_DIR . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . 'content.zip' and BackupController streamed then unlinked that file. Follow-up members a9606c4e (throw on ZipArchive open failure) and 7c055785 (return-type cleanup) kept the same path. GitHub squash-merged the PR as 2cd1dac0ce70b28500a4845f2105c42f82b87a50 onto main. git blame on 4.1.6 still attributes the zipFile assignment to that squash; later refactors (b62cda109, 323aafff05, 7a57114880) did not relocate the archive. Thorsten's 2026-08-02 fix ad858dfb3 (4.1) / 76a6eec23 (main) switched the write to tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), 'pmf_content_backup_') and BinaryFileResponse::deleteFileAfterSend().

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-75920 is a published (not rejected) VulnCheck CVE mirroring first-party GHSA-8hmh-mrx6-pqvf. The mechanism is CWE-377: Backup::createContentFolderBackup() wrote a sensitive content/ ZIP to document-root content.zip and BackupController unlinked only after streaming, so unauthenticated GET /content.zip could win a race. Vendor advisory 2026-08-04 and the 4.1.6 vs 4.1.7 trees confirm a real bug through 4.1.6, patched in 4.1.7 (CVE's 'before v4.1.6' / 4.1.6-unaffected listing is a range error, not a withdrawn/false advisory). BIC search used -S content.zip and the first-party file/function names, not an AI-commit hunt. The default-branch first appearance is GitHub squash 2cd1dac0 (PR #3003). That squash is not the BIC; its three public members were reconstructed from the PR. The smallest first-write of $zipFile = PMF_ROOT_DIR . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . 'content.zip' and the download/unlink path is member d28770dc; its parent 34e30bd2 was verified in the clone to lack those symbols. Later members and 2025 refactors did not change the web-root location, so they are not the introducer. AI judgment is from the BIC commit object only: Jan authored and committed d28770dc with a one-line feat subject and no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot markers. The squash landing is also unmarked. Therefore a real vulnerability with human authorship: NOT_AI. Fix SHA is the 4.1-line commit ad858dfb3 that 4.1.7 actually contains (main equivalent 76a6eec23 is the same change, later the same day).
